elements.element: Frequency limited to no more than once per 12 months
elements.evidence: "(i) no more than once in any twelve (12) month period"

elements.element: At least 30 days' prior written notice
elements.evidence: "(ii) upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Customer ... except where IBM reasonably believes an emergency or unlawful activity exists" — the notice requirement is disapplied whenever IBM believes 'unlawful activity' exists, which is the very subject of a Subsection 11.2(b) warranty investigation
"and during normal business hours, except where IBM reasonably believes an emergency or unlawful activity exists" — same self-judged carve-out swallows the limit

elements.element: Performed by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality
elements.evidence: "(iii) by IBM or an independent auditor bound by confidentiality obligations" — permits IBM itself to audit, so independence is optional

elements.element: Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%
elements.evidence: "(v) at IBM's expense, unless the investigation reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding five percent (5%) of amounts due"

elements.element: No direct access to Customer systems
elements.evidence: "(iv) without direct or remote access to Customer's systems, networks, premises or Customer Components"
"no more than once in any twelve (12) month period"
30 days is stated, but is excused "where IBM reasonably believes an emergency or unlawful activity exists", so no minimum notice is assured

elements.element: Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%
elements.evidence: "unless the investigation reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding five percent (5%)" — cost-shift trigger set at 5%, below the fallback's 10%

offending_extra_words: except where IBM reasonably believes an emergency or unlawful activity exists
obligations no less protective than those in this Agreement
reasons: Preferred fails on the independent-auditor element: "by IBM or an independent auditor" lets IBM self-audit, which is not the playbook position of an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.

Preferred also fails on notice and business hours because the inserted carve-out "except where IBM reasonably believes an emergency or unlawful activity exists" is judged by IBM alone and covers precisely the suspected-misuse scenario the investigation right addresses, so the 30-day/business-hours protections can be bypassed at will.
Fallback is not independently satisfied: the cost-shift threshold is set at the preferred 5% rather than the fallback 10%, and the notice minimum is again subject to the self-judged exception.

Minimality fails: the edit expands 16 words to 116 (7.25x) with a changed-character ratio of 0.846, and adds unnecessary breadth ('unlawful activity' exception, 'networks, premises or Customer Components', 'no less protective than those in this Agreement') where a tighter proviso listing frequency, notice, auditor, access and cost would suffice.

Intent is impaired by duplication and internal tension with the retained sentence "Except in an emergency or as may otherwise be required by law, before undertaking the activities in Subsection 11.3(a) or 11.3(b), IBM will attempt to notify Customer" — two differently worded emergency/notice mechanics now sit in the same clause.

Fix: delete "IBM or" and the "unlawful activity" carve-out (leave at most a narrow emergency exception consistent with the existing sentence), and keep the 5% figure only if targeting preferred with all other preferred elements intact.
